twinSimulator.pageSubtitle: Enter a few monthly numbers and see three versions of your future — one where nothing changes, one where you tighten up, and one where costs creep up or something unexpected hits.
twinSimulator.introBody: This isn't a forecast, it's a place to try things out. Use it to see which everyday choices move the needle most on your savings, your debt, and your goal.
twinSimulator.formHelper: Rough numbers are fine. What matters is that they're close to real life, not that they're exact.
twinSimulator.summaryHelper: Each row shows where you'd land by the end of your timeline. Money after debt is your savings and investments minus whatever you still owe.
twinSimulator.chartTitle: Money After Debt, Month by Month
twinSimulator.chartHelper: Savings minus debt, tracked over time. The higher the line, the more room you have to fund goals or absorb a surprise.
twinSimulator.disclaimerBody: This tool is for learning and planning only. It doesn't recommend financial products, promise returns, or replace advice from a qualified professional.
twinSimulator.noResultText: Run the simulation to compare your current habits with a better version and a riskier one.

current.title: Current habits
current.body: Uses your income, spending, debt payments, and savings exactly as you entered them.

improved.title: Better habits
improved.body: Trims lifestyle spending by 20% and food and transport by 10%. If you're still carrying debt, 60% of the freed-up cash goes there and 40% goes to savings.

risky.title: Riskier path
risky.body: Pushes flexible spending up and throws in one surprise cost along the way, so you can see how well the plan holds up.

fields.riskBehavior: Risk setting for the riskier path

fieldHelp.monthlyIncome: Use the amount that actually reaches your account each month.
fieldHelp.currentSavings: Cash, savings, and investments you could actually put toward this goal.
fieldHelp.essentialSpending: Rent, bills, school fees, insurance — the things you can't easily skip.
fieldHelp.lifestyleSpending: Eating out, entertainment, hobbies, shopping, subscriptions, and treats.
fieldHelp.foodTransportSpending: Regular meals, groceries, commuting, ride-hailing, fuel, and parking.
fieldHelp.otherSpending: Any other monthly cost that doesn't fit the categories above.
fieldHelp.debtBalance: What you still owe across loans, credit cards, installments, and paylater.
fieldHelp.monthlyDebtPayment: What you usually put toward debt each month.
fieldHelp.goalAmount: How much you want to have saved by the end of your timeline.
fieldHelp.timeHorizon: How many months ahead you want to look.
fieldHelp.expectedReturn: A rough yearly growth rate for your savings or investments. Enter 0 to leave growth out of it.
fieldHelp.riskBehavior: Sets how much extra spending and how big a surprise cost the riskier path assumes.

biggestBottleneck.overspending: Flexible spending is your biggest drag. Too much of each paycheck goes out the door before it can turn into savings or debt paid off.
biggestBottleneck.highDebt: Debt is your biggest drag. A large share of your cash flow goes to repayments instead of your goal.
biggestBottleneck.shortHorizon: Your goal may be too big for the time you've given it. The plan works, it just needs more months.
biggestBottleneck.lowIncome: Your income is stretched thin against this goal and your monthly costs. Cutting back helps, but earning more may be the bigger lever.
biggestBottleneck.alreadyAtGoal: You've already saved enough for this goal. The next step is protecting it and deciding where the extra cash should go.
biggestBottleneck.noSavingsCapacity: There's almost nothing left each month once spending and debt payments are covered. You'll need some breathing room before the plan can go anywhere.

bestNextAction.cutLifestyleSpending: Pick one or two flexible costs to cut, and send that money straight to savings or debt. Small changes you repeat every month matter most here.
bestNextAction.buildEmergencyFund: Build an emergency buffer first, so one surprise bill doesn't knock the plan off course.
bestNextAction.focusOnDebt: Go after the most expensive debt first and keep the payments steady. Every bit you clear makes the months that follow easier.
bestNextAction.extendHorizon: Give the goal more time, or break it into smaller milestones. Either way the monthly number gets more realistic.
bestNextAction.increaseIncome: Look for extra income while holding your spending steady. A raise only helps if it doesn't get spent.
bestNextAction.maintainGoodHabits: You're in good shape. Keep the habit going, protect what you've built, and check back on the plan now and then.

first.name: Danny Sudarsono
first.testimony: As a corporate professional who is also building a startup, I feel that Docduit can provide financial advice comparable to top-tier wealth management services. It's quite cool to get AI-based advice from Docduit.

second.name: Hasna Luthfiana
second.testimony: As a new jobber, I feel very helped by the Docduit website! Consulting with AI makes me feel more comfortable talking about my financial conditions. I often felt confused about who to ask when faced with financial problems. But with Docduit, I can get new insights and relevant advice without feeling awkward. As I'm still learning to manage finances at the start of my career, Docduit is truly the right solution.

third.name: Azka Adziman
third.occupation: Undergraduate Student at Oxford University | Clash of Champions Season 3
third.testimony: As a university student, Docduit's financial calculators are certainly very useful. They not only break down the targets you need to achieve each month, but also recommend investment tools that can help you achieve your dreams faster, such as foreign currency and gold. If you want to buy a new gadget or save for a vacation, you should try Docduit!
